hints: Write z=x+iy and multiply (z+4)/(z+4i) by the conjugate of its denominator.
Set the imaginary part of the numerator to zero to obtain a linear relation between x and y.
Combine that relation with x²+y²=10, solve the resulting quadratic, and form both answers as x+iy.
Check the denominator is non-zero and each quotient is real.
walkthrough:
Let $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$, where $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$. Express the quotient in terms of $x$ and $y$:
$$\dfrac{z + 4}{z + 4\mathrm{i}} = \dfrac{(x + 4) + \mathrm{i}y}{x + \mathrm{i}(y + 4)}$$

Multiply numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate of the denominator, $x - \mathrm{i}(y + 4)$:
$$\dfrac{[(x + 4) + \mathrm{i}y][x - \mathrm{i}(y + 4)]}{x^2 + (y + 4)^2}$$

Expand the numerator:
$$[(x + 4) + \mathrm{i}y][x - \mathrm{i}(y + 4)] = x(x + 4) - \mathrm{i}(x + 4)(y + 4) + \mathrm{i}xy - \mathrm{i}^2 y(y + 4)$$
$$= [x(x + 4) + y(y + 4)] + \mathrm{i}[xy - (xy + 4x + 4y + 16)]$$
$$= [x(x + 4) + y(y + 4)] - \mathrm{i}(4x + 4y + 16)$$

Since the quotient is real, set the imaginary part of the numerator equal to zero:
$$-(4x + 4y + 16) = 0 \implies 4x + 4y + 16 = 0 \implies x + y = -4$$
$$y = -x - 4$$

Substitute $y = -x - 4$ into the modulus condition $|z| = \sqrt{10} \implies x^2 + y^2 = 10$:
$$x^2 + (-x - 4)^2 = 10$$
$$x^2 + (x^2 + 8x + 16) = 10$$
$$2x^2 + 8x + 6 = 0$$
$$x^2 + 4x + 3 = 0$$

Factor the quadratic equation in $x$:
$$(x + 1)(x + 3) = 0$$
$$x = -1 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -3$$

Find the corresponding values of $y$ using $y = -x - 4$:
$$\text{When } x = -1: \quad y = -(-1) - 4 = 1 - 4 = -3 \implies z = -1 - 3\mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{When } x = -3: \quad y = -(-3) - 4 = 3 - 4 = -1 \implies z = -3 - \mathrm{i}$$
